after.name: Uruk siege in Gilgamesh and Aga poem: historical basis and date uncertain

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Wikidata Q3204978 calls this Siege of Uruk and lists 27th-century start and end with zero references, not a specific year. The Old Babylonian poem Gilgamesh and Aga portrays a Kishite siege, yet the linked article says the war’s historicity remains open and notes a proposed c.2600 date. The Met says no contemporary information is known about Gilgamesh, who may have been a historical figure. The inherited -2701 slot is an arbitrary game reference: neither the siege, composition nor the poem’s recorded events are verified in that year. Existing latitude marks the archaeological Uruk site; the radius is a game reference, not a battlefield footprint. A literary narrative is not proof of individual actions or casualty counts. The wikidata-more pack may use a different end convention in NewsIndex; this note may also appear at the stored end year. No troop or political effect is supported.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: One inherited reference slot, not a verified historical date; the literary text is preserved later.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Inherited Uruk site reference, not verified siege position or battlefield extent.
